results.content: Often, a system can be changed to accept energy more efficiently, by adding an element called an “impedance matcher.” Most people have never heard of an impedance matcher, but once you know about them, you begin to see them everywhere: in the shape of a trumpet, the anti-reflective coating on a lens, and the foam spikes on the inside of a recording booth. Although born in physiology, it is likely that the idea of allostasis in the coming years can become important as an umbrella for trends currently fermenting in the understanding of the mind. Affordances are “what the environment offers the animal for good or ill,” according to Gibson, and “the information is in the light.” (Gibson, like most psychologists and philosophers of perception, concentrated on vision.)  While many researchers and theoreticians in the fledgling interdisciplinary field of cognitive science found Gibson’s basic idea of affordances compelling, Gibson and his more radical followers managed to create a cult-like aura around his ideas, repelling many otherwise interested thinkers.

results.title: Imaging, Spectroscopy, and Beyond XI, Conference Details
results.content: In response, significant advancements have been made in high-speed optical sensing with high sensitivity and large dynamic ranges suitable for single biomolecule measurements, high-speed optical spectroscopy with superior spectral resolution and broad spectral ranges for monitoring rapid molecular dynamics, and high-speed optical imaging with high spatial resolution and the ability to capture multidimensional images for observing structural changes in biological systems and analyzing large heterogeneous populations of cells. Electro-optic fluorescence lifetime microscopy (EO-FLIM) has emerged as a high-speed FLIM technique, utilizing an electro-optic modulator as a gating unit to achieve fluorescence lifetime imaging at kilohertz frame rates and enabling the measurement of rapid cellular signals. High-throughput applications suffer from the trade-off between resolution and field of view (FOV), an inherent feature of lenses used in free space optics imaging systems. Here, we introduce a state-of-the-art two-photon microscopy system capable of single-cell resolution imaging across an ultra-large field of view exceeding 50 mm², enabling in vivo imaging across multiple brain areas.
